A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Balanced Neural ODE research, retaining matching methods, case studies, and appendix derivations. Text extraction and visual inspection covered both complete documents, including figures, tables, and appendices, without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original VAE and B-NODE experiments, including heat-flow reconstruction and generalization, power-plant accuracy and runtime, Koopman approximation, and appendix latent-channel analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds nonlinear and linear surrogate benchmarks, B-NODE masking experiments, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The encoders, Gaussian latent distributions, continuous propagation of variational parameters, stochastic training, ELBO objective, and linear Koopman variants remain unchanged. The new masking and architectural variations are supplementary experiments, rather than revisions to the proposed core procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds controlled robot dynamics from MuJoCo Ant, pressure-wave dynamics from Water Hammer, and three-dimensional airflow from Small Grid (Sections 4.3, 5.3, and A.5.6–A.5.8). These substantially broaden the evaluated domains beyond the retained thermal examples and analytic Koopman system.

E2.justification: Table 2 introduces evaluated eDMDc and DMDc comparisons for linear surrogates. Table 1 adds zero-β B-NODE controls and changes comparator membership on retained tasks, including SS-NODE on heat flow and input-conditioned Latent NODE on the power plant. These extend v1's heat-flow TBR/Latent ODE and power-plant SS-NODE comparisons.

E3.justification: New benchmark protocols specify variance-normalized RMSE, with power-plant outputs evaluated in the nonlinear benchmark and states in the linear benchmark (A.5.9–A.5.10); retained plots use mean normalization. Added experiments introduce MuJoCo sequence/feature filtering, DMD rank and observable searches, and masking/retraining and sensitivity controls. These are new evaluation designs, not demonstrated changes to existing accuracy experiments.

E4.justification: A.6.1 newly tests masking low-KL channels in linear and nonlinear B-NODEs, followed by training with β set to zero. This differs from the retained static VAE masking analysis in A.3.3. A.6.2 adds sensitivity tests covering network depth and width, activations, decoder controls, latent capacity, solver tolerances, and β.

E5.justification: No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. The existing latent-distribution variability visualization remains, while the added benchmark and sensitivity tables report point estimates without run-level uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, Table 4, and Figure A.10 add substantial results. For example, Table 2 reports power-plant RMSE 0.20 for both B-NODE β=0.01 with 25 states and eDMDc with 45 states. Figure 6b replaces B-NODE CPU timing of 4.1 seconds with 0.5 seconds and SS-NODE GPU timing of 15.5 seconds with 68 seconds; the expanded solver and batch descriptions prevent treating these as established same-setting performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The probabilistic factorizations, ELBO derivations, KL decomposition, and Koopman equations are retained. The Gaussian KL formula newly displayed in Section 2.2 already appears in v1 Appendix A.3.1. Expanded explanations of independence and fixed priors do not establish a substantive change to the existing mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim input-driven surrogate modeling with automatically reduced latent dimensionality, continuous propagation of variational parameters, stochastic stabilization, and Koopman approximation. The expanded benchmark examples and condensed conclusion change supporting evidence and emphasis without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v1's discussion emphasizes real-data inference requirements, unresolved uncertainty-quantification applications, and numerical stability. v3 replaces this with comparative accuracy, automation, speed, and applicability arguments, and removes explicit dynamic-variance training caveats from Section 3.4. It also adds interpretations connecting fewer function evaluations to speed and masking results to persistent dimensionality reduction.

D1.justification: A.5.6–A.5.10 add dataset construction settings, MuJoCo filtering, PyKoopman implementation information, DMD rank searches, and radial-basis-function tuning. Small Grid and Water Hammer models or datasets are stated to be available on request. A.5.4 newly documents final-stage dopri5 training and adaptive batch step-size control; the main code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting PyKoopman, Gymnasium/Minari, and the Water Hammer example, while removing the Koopman VAE discussion and citation and the hybrid-modeling reference to Thummerer and Mikelsons. The broader positioning relative to Neural ODEs, DVAEs, model reduction, and Koopman theory remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the motivation and KL-channel explanation, standardize SS-NODE terminology, replace the discussion/future-work text, and condense the conclusion. Benchmark subsections are added, but the overall background–method–applications progression and most existing method and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables and Figures A.8–A.10. Figure 6b is redesigned with an additional CPU comparison, speedup factors, and ODE-evaluation counts. Several retained figures are relocated or resized, and plot annotations are revised. This substantially expands and reorganizes the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: Table 2 supplies the DMD comparisons explicitly left for future work in v1, while Table 1 broadens comparative validation across distinct dynamics. The new B-NODE masking and sensitivity experiments directly strengthen evidence for the central dimensionality-reduction claim. Removing useful stability and real-data caveats weakens qualification, and timing comparisons require care, but the improved comparative and diagnostic evidence substantially strengthens the paper overall.
